document.title: Closing Disclosure / settlement statement for a real estate sale

boxes.label: Contract sales price for the whole property
Seller's selling expenses: sales commissions, advertising fees, legal fees, loan charges the seller paid that would normally have been the buyer's, and other fees or costs to sell
boxes.notes: ONLY selling expenses are code E on Form 8949. A credit the seller gives the buyer, a proration of taxes or dues, and the payoff of the seller's own loan are NOT selling expenses and are not this box (F-494). The box name is kept because stored confirmations are keyed on it. The p523 text reads: 'Determine your selling expenses. These are the costs directly associated with selling your home.' (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/p523--2025.pdf).

boxes.label: Every transferor named on the statement

boxes.box: real estate taxes allocated to the seller
boxes.label: Seller's share of the real estate taxes for the year of sale (the proration through the day before the sale)
boxes.notes: Deductible by the seller as real estate tax; where the buyer paid them they are also part of the sale price. The p523 text reads: 'Any real estate taxes the buyer paid on your behalf' (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/p523--2025.pdf).

boxes.label: Points the buyer paid on the purchase loan, as shown on the settlement statement
boxes.notes: The buyer's side of the statement. The i1040sca text reads: 'Points are shown on your settlement statement.' (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/i1040sca--2025.pdf).

document.notes: NO ROUTABLE BOX, AND REQUIRED ANYWAY. It is the ONLY document that can settle whether Form 1099-S box 2 is this seller's share or the whole unallocated proceeds, and the only source of the selling expenses that become a Form 8949 column (g) adjustment under code E. Its boxes feed facts, not lines. A settlement statement carrying no form number can be the sole source of a reportable figure — the Form 8949 instructions require the transaction to be reported 'even if you didn't receive a Form 1099-B, Form 1099-DA, or Form 1099-S'.

extraction.note: A taxpayer's own record. No prescribed layout, so no structured model and no boxes to read: it prints ITEMS in the client's own words, and which declared box each belongs in is a JUDGEMENT a person confirms (spec 075 group D, clarification Q1). Read by the declared custom model in TRANSCRIBE mode - the same reader, a second template - which copies every line verbatim and names no destination. A separate, cheap proposal call then suggests a box per item; **only a box a person confirms places anything**, so an engagement with nineteen rental sheets shows an empty Schedule E until somebody has looked. That is the decision, not a defect.

custom.reads: a settlement statement from a property sale or purchase (a Closing Disclosure, ALTA statement or HUD-1)

boxes: real estate taxes allocated to the seller
